levels.title: Curiosity
levels.blurb: At 15, I learned Python to build games. I didn’t know it yet, but that curiosity became the foundation for everything I do now.
highlights: First self-taught programming fundamentals
Early interest in building and experimenting
Huge interest in technology and how things work under the hood

image.alt: Pixel scene: teen coding at night

levels.title: Foundations
levels.blurb: Coming to the U.S., I started from the basics—hardware, systems, and how computers work in the real world. That’s where I learned to troubleshoot and think step-by-step.
highlights: Hands-on hardware + system fundamentals
Practical troubleshooting mindset
Built confidence through real labs

image.alt: Pixel scene: PC parts and cables on desk

levels.title: Networking Era
levels.blurb: Networking taught me structure. I built and tested networks in Packet Tracer, learned routing concepts, and got comfortable diagnosing problems like an engineer.
highlights: Cisco Packet Tracer projects
Network fundamentals and troubleshooting
Learned to document and explain systems

image.alt: Pixel scene: network diagram on screen

levels.title: Cyber Discovery
levels.blurb: I transferred to FIU and switched to cybersecurity. I explored both blue and red team paths and started building my own learning environment to train consistently.
highlights: Major switch into cybersecurity
Home lab built using virtualization (VirtualBox, vulnerable VMs and Kali Linux)
Started exploring security pathways (red vs blue) and finding my focus

image.alt: Pixel scene: Kali terminal on laptop

levels.title: Acceleration
levels.blurb: This is where things accelerated. I earned Security+ certification, had my first blue team competition experience under red team pressure, more skillful and more stronger in Cybersecurity.
highlights: CompTIA Security+ certification
Built deeper blue team skills (SIEM, incident response, forensics)
First blue team competition experience (CCDC) as participant.

image.alt: Pixel scene: alerts and logs on screen

levels.title: Being a hardware lab and course learning assistant
levels.blurb: Teaching changed my confidence and mindset. Now, I understand why tech should be easier to understand by people who are far from it.
highlights: Tutored students in multiple courses (programming, hardware, networking, cybersecurity)
Supported lab environments (Linux/Windows)
Built skill of explaining complex concepts in simple terms

image.alt: Pixel scene: helping students at a lab desk

levels.title: AWS & Cloud
levels.blurb: I fell in love with cloud because it connects architecture and security. To understand security deeply, I committed to learning AWS from the inside out.
highlights: AWS deep dive (architecture + services)
Passed AWS Solutions Architect Associate certification
Shift toward cloud security engineering

image.alt: Pixel scene: cloud architecture blocks on screen

levels.title: AI & Research
levels.blurb: I worked on AI model evaluation and then joined a research effort using AI to identify security gaps early—before code exists.
highlights: AI fellowship with Handshake AI, understaning model evaluation and limitations
Research: AI-Assisted assurance case for security requirement completeness in defense critical infrastructure
Exploring how AI can help identify security gaps early in the development lifecycle

image.alt: Pixel scene: AI nodes and documents on screen

levels.title: CCDC Captain
levels.blurb: We had five members and one week. We competed anyway. I led the team, kept everyone focused, and we placed 16th out of 45—fighting until the last minute.
highlights: Second time competing in CCDC, this time as team captain
Undersized team (5 vs expected 12) and only one week to prepare
Placed 16th out of 45 teams

image.alt: Pixel scene: scoreboard and mission notes

levels.title: Integration
levels.blurb: Today, I work at the intersection of cloud, security engineering, and applied AI. I focus on building systems that are secure, cost-effective and using latest AI capabilities.
highlights: Cloud architecture with security-first thinking
AI for faster and smarter solutions
Confident and ready to be part of a team make a bigger impact in the world of technology
Passion for learning more and more, staying up-to-date with the latest technologies and trends in the field

image.alt: Pixel scene: unified cloud, shield, and AI nodes on one desk
